art.subject: Black-winged Cuckooshrike (Lalage melaschistos), adult male: plumage medium slate-grey with a bluish tone, darkest on the lores and around the eye; no crest, the crown feathers lie flat; wings blackish, the flight feathers black and the wing coverts dark slate-grey, the whole wing clearly darker than the body; underparts grey, paler on the belly and whitish on the undertail coverts; tail black, long and graduated, the outer feathers broadly tipped white, giving a chequered look from below; bill short, black and slightly hooked; iris dark reddish-brown; legs blackish.
art.pose: perched on an open branch at a forest edge, side view
art.scene: Korean forest clearing beside an orchard; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view perched: slate-grey body with a bluish tone, darker lores and face, dark reddish-brown eye, blackish wings clearly darker than the body, long graduated black tail with white tips to the outer feathers, short black bill
adult female, side view perched: paler grey than the male on the head and back, with a whitish broken eye-ring and faint pale barring on the lower underparts, wings and tail blackish
adult, in flight seen from below, head, body and tail in line: grey body, black flight feathers with a white patch at the base of the primaries, white-tipped outer tail feathers
art.build: Slender, medium-small songbird, 19–24cm, a little smaller and slimmer than Brown-eared Bulbul, with a rounded head with no crest (the crown feathers lie flat), a short neck and a long, graduated tail. Bill black, shorter than the head, fairly stout with a slightly hooked tip. Legs short and dark. In flight shows a small white patch under the base of the primaries and white tips to the outer tail feathers. Sits quietly in the canopy, often on open branches.
avoid: Do not paint white underparts or a white forehead; those suit Ashy Minivet (Pericrocotus divaricatus).
Do not paint a forked tail or an all-black body; that is Black Drongo.
Do not paint a grey tail; it is black with white tips to the outer feathers.
Do not give it a black eye mask or a heavy shrike bill.
